title: introduce-economic-compass-prefill-suggester-and-compact-quant-profiles
author: Maya Hernandez
description:
Motivation: customers frequently ask for better out-of-the-box cost controls that balance latency SLOs with unit economics. This PR introduces the "Economic Compass" runtime component: a prefill/batching suggester that generates tenant-specific default batch/cache/quantization presets and a small set of compact quant profiles validated against representative workloads.

What this change does: Adds a heuristics engine that: 1) samples incoming tenant traffic patterns (shape, sequence length distribution, rate), 2) synthesizes candidate prefill and batching defaults, 3) picks compact quant profiles (fp16/q4/q8_float-like variants) ranked by estimated unit cost uplift vs. quality score, and 4) writes a recommended defaults manifest that the Console and CLI can apply as a tenant-level default. The engine includes a lightweight simulator that runs inexpensive token-cost/latency estimates so admins can dry-run suggestions before applying them.

Key components in this PR: - runtime/econ/compass: heuristics, sampling adapters, and a small internal simulator (Python + Rust FFI wrapper) - configs/presets/tenant_defaults_v2.yaml: schema for recommended defaults and quant profiles - console-api: endpoints to preview and apply suggestions (with preview diffs) - telemetry: unit-econ traces and a new metric econ.suggestion.score - cli: redwood-ctl econ preview/apply commands - docs: guide and examples for common workloads

Checklist: - [x] Heuristics for batch/cache suggested defaults implemented - [x] Compact quant profile selection and safety fallback implemented - [x] Unit-econ estimator integrated with telemetry - [x] API + CLI preview/apply paths - [x] End-to-end tests for simulator and CI smoke tests - [x] Docs and admin example walkthroughs

Related: shares goals with ENG-6123 (tenant warmstart) but focuses on defaults discovery rather than real-time warmup. SUP-1201 surfaced a customer incident where naive quant swaps caused quality regressions; this PR includes a conservative rollback path and a quality-score delta threshold to avoid risky autosuggestions.

Risks and mitigations: The suggestions are conservative by default (apply only as "recommended" until operator confirms). Quant swaps are only suggested for models with eval baselines and require a manual opt-in in tenant settings or an explicit CLI apply. Simulator uses historical traces only and caps synthetic batch sizes to avoid unrealistic shapes.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Large PR, can we split simulator FFI into a separate follow-up? The Rust sim adds complexity to runtime builds.
Maya Hernandez: Answered: simulator is optional at build time and packaged as a wasm artifact for hosted. Added BUILD.md explaining packaging; kept FFI to enable local dev performance.
Sofia Grant: The quant profile selection needs a clear safety gate — prefer only recommending q4 variants for now.
Maya Hernandez: Adjusted scoring to prefer fp16/q4 variants and added an apply-time confirmation with a quality delta threshold (default 0.02).
Liam O'Connor: CI flake on e2e/test_econ_suggester.py — failing under noisy parallel runs.
Maya Hernandez: Investigated and added retry + stabilized test harness; re-ran CI.
Sofia Grant: Approving once docs include tenant opt-in screenshots and an operator rollback doc.
Maya Hernandez: Added docs/ops/econ-compass.md covering screenshots and rollback steps.
ci_summary: All checks passed after test stabilization. Smoke pipeline showed one transient failure (simulator build) that was fixed by separating wasm packaging. Unit and integration tests: pass. E2E lightweight suite: pass.
release_notes: Added Economic Compass: tenant prefill suggester that recommends batching, cache, and compact quantization profiles with a dry-run simulator and safe apply workflow. Operators can preview before applying. Introduces econ.suggestion.score telemetry and CLI commands redwood-ctl econ preview/apply.
additional_notes: This PR intentionally ships suggested defaults as non-destructive "recommended" entries in tenant manifests. Follow-ups planned: 1) auto-rollout experiment pipeline (A/B) 2) richer quality evaluators integration 3) UI for bulk-apply across tenants.
